lines.text: A hundred men versus one gorilla. The internet has been arguing about this for months.
lines.note: Cartoon simulation · not a real fight

lines.text: The men charge. All at once.
A silverback weighs around 160 kilos. One swing, and ten men go flying.
lines.note: Wild adult male gorillas: roughly 140–200 kg

lines.text: People say gorillas are ten times stronger than us. Fun fact: nobody has ever actually measured it.
lines.note: Berggorilla & Regenwald Direkthilfe: no study has measured gorilla vs human strength

lines.text: Doesn't matter. Twenty more go down. Then thirty. But he's getting tired.
So he does the one thing gorillas actually do. He beats his chest.
lines.note: Wright et al. 2021 (Scientific Reports): chest beats advertise body size

lines.text: That sound tells rivals exactly how big he is. And the last forty men run.
lines.note: Bigger silverbacks make deeper chest beats

lines.text: He never wanted the fight. He wanted lunch. About twenty kilos of leaves.
lines.note: Wild silverbacks eat roughly 18–30 kg of plants a day

lines.text: Winner? The gorilla. And the internet is still arguing.
